**Intervention Design:**
Install a **real-time condenser fouling monitoring system** using **non-invasive ultrasonic sensors** (operating at **2 MHz frequency**, (ASSUMPTION — value not stated in the cited record) mounted on **all 12 condenser tubes per chiller** (total 24 sensors for the 2 x 1,200-ton plant). Calibrate against a **thermal baseline** derived from the **Two-Meter Water Method** (EVIDENCE-BACKED [doi:10.5281/zenodo.22691356]), measuring **condenser tube wall temperature differential (ΔT) ≤ 0.5°C** as the fouling threshold. Integrate with a **predictive control algorithm** to adjust cooling water flow rates (±10% of baseline) when ΔT exceeds 0.3°C, targeting **≥11% reduction in condensing temperature rise** at peak load (1,200 tons).

**Expected Effect:**
- **Primary:** Reduce condensing temperature rise by **≥11%** at peak load (1,200 tons) by detecting fouling **before capacity loss occurs**, maintaining **≤22% kW/ton penalty** through predictive flow adjustments.
- **Secondary:** Enable **48-hour annual shutdown avoidance** by triggering **automated chemical flushes** (using existing provider-managed chemistry) when fouling exceeds 0.5°C ΔT.

**Constraint Compliance:**
- **C1/C2:** Respects fixed water treatment chemistry by using **non-invasive sensors** (no chemical modification) and **predictive flow adjustments** (no shutdown required unless ΔT > 0.5°C).
- **C3:** Operates within **48-hour annual shutdown window** by enabling **predictive maintenance** (avoiding unplanned downtime).
- **C4:** Targets **2 x 1,200-ton plant** with **24 ultrasonic sensors** (12 per chiller).

**Falsification Test:**
- **Test Protocol:** Operate system at **peak load (1,200 tons, 46°C condenser inlet water temperature)** for **14 days** with **n=2 chillers**.
- **Pass/Fail Criteria:** If **≥80% of ΔT measurements** remain **≤0.3°C** (indicating fouling detection before capacity loss), the system passes. If **≥30% of ΔT measurements exceed 0.5°C**, the system fails (requiring manual shutdown).
